An Example of Analytic Shinydashboard: Regression Modeling

Cheng Peng

West Chester University

1 Introduction

1.1 Dataset Overview

The Iris dataset is one of the most famous and widely used datasets in statistics and machine learning. Originally introduced by the British statistician and biologist Ronald Fisher in 1936, it serves as a classic example for discriminant analysis and pattern recognition.

1.2 Data Characteristics

The dataset contains measurements of 150 iris flowers from three different species:

Species Number of Samples
Setosa 50
Versicolor 50
Virginica 50

1.3 Variables

The dataset includes four numerical variables (measured in centimeters) and one categorical variable:

Variable Name Type Unit Description
Sepal Length Numerical cm Length of the sepal (in centimeters)
Sepal Width Numerical cm Width of the sepal (in centimeters)
Petal Length Numerical cm Length of the petal (in centimeters)
Petal Width Numerical cm Width of the petal (in centimeters)
Species Categorical — Species of iris (Setosa, Versicolor, Virginica)

2 Interactive Dashboard for SLR

2.1 Dashboard Overview

The dashboard is developed using R Shiny and ShinyDashboard, providing an interactive environment for exploring simple linear regression relationships among the numerical variables in the Iris dataset. The application can be accessed through any web browser and offers real-time model fitting and visualization.

Control Description Options
Species Selector Filters data by species All Species, Setosa, Versicolor, Virginica
Response Variable (Y) Selects the dependent variable Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length, Petal.Width
Predictor Variable (X) Selects the independent variable Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length, Petal.Width
New X Value Specifies value for prediction Numeric input (range: 0-10)

2.2 Visualization Panels

Panel 1: Scatter Plot with Regression & Prediction

  • Displays the relationship between X and Y variables

  • Points are color-coded by species (when “All Species” is selected)

  • Includes the regression line (orange)

  • Highlights the prediction point (yellow star)

  • Interactive hover for data point details

Panel 2: Residual Plot

  • Shows residuals vs. fitted values

  • Includes a zero reference line (purple dashed)

  • Points are color-coded by species

  • Useful for checking homoscedasticity and independence assumptions

Panel 3: Distribution Plot (Kernel Density)

  • Displays kernel density estimates of the response variable

  • Overlays density curves for different species

  • Shows distribution patterns across species

Panel 4: Model Summary Table

  • Regression Coefficients: Intercept, slope, standard errors, t-values, and p-values

  • Goodness-of-Fit Measures: \(R^2\), adjusted \(R^2\), residual standard error, F-statistic, and p-value

2.3 Technical Implementation

  • Reactive Programming: The dashboard uses Shiny’s reactive expressions to automatically update all outputs when user inputs change.

  • Automatic Variable Validation: When a user selects the same variable as both predictor and response, the system automatically suggests an alternative predictor variable.

  • Prediction Functionality: Users can input a new X value and see the predicted Y value with 95% prediction interval.

  • Interactive Graphics: Utilizes plotly for interactive visualizations with zoom, pan, and hover capabilities.
